slides.title: SocioVerse2: A Longitudinal Dynamic Social Simulation Framework under a Human-AI Co-evolutionary Paradigm
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC SOCIAL SIMULATION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: SocioVerse2 introduces a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm for longitudinal social simulation and counterfactual interventions, supporting the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: SocioVerse2 is a longitudinal social simulation framework enabling human-AI co-evolution through controllable research and simulation loops.
card.key_idea: It uses a 'two loops, one infrastructure' paradigm: a longitudinal simulation loop for counterfactual branching via interventions and a controllable research loop for iterative study state editing.
card.evaluation: Validated across three case families and seven studies, including reproducing ABMs, policy modeling, and macro-economic index nowcasting using real-world grounding.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Agent-based Modeling: Equilibrium, Echo Chambers, and Efficiency in Hybrid Coevolutionary Opinion Games
slides.tldr: LLM-DRIVEN AGENTS IN COEVOLUTIONARY OPINION GAMES
slides.highlight: This work introduces the Hybrid Coevolutionary Opinion Game (H-COG) to analyze the equilibrium and social cost of LLM-driven agents in dynamic networks, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLM-driven agents are five times less efficient than analytical agents in coevolutionary opinion games.
card.key_idea: The H-COG framework integrates cost-minimizing Friedkin–Johnsen agents and Phi-4 LLM agents in a dynamically rewiring network, measuring efficiency via social cost and Price of Anarchy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 5,199 Reddit comments, three initial topologies, and nine mixing levels; results show LLM agents are less polarized but more inefficient.
card.limitation: LLM agents are displaced from their own prior positions rather than merely disagreeing with neighbors, driving inefficiency.

slides.title: Multimodal Voice Activity Projection for Social Robot Mediation: Expected Behavior and Deployment Constraints
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL TURN-TAKING PREDICTION FOR ROBOT MEDIATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a perception layer that estimates conversational floor evolution and turn-taking events using audio-visual evidence, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MM-VAP predicts future conversational floor dynamics to help social robots mediate human-human interactions via gaze.
card.key_idea: Uses pretrained audio-visual encoders (TalkNet/WhisperFlamingo) with LoRA adaptation and inter-speaker attention to project future voice activity states and infer turn-taking events zero-shot.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NoXi, NoXi+J, and Haru EDR datasets using F1-scores; pretrained backbones significantly outperformed the CPC+3DResNet baseline.
card.limitation: Real-time deployment constraints, including preprocessing latency, multimodal synchronization, and hardware limitations, remain unsolved open problems.

slides.title: Listening and Mirroring: The Effects of Verbal Attunement and Behavioral Mimicry on Social and Empathic Perceptions of Embodied AI Agents in VR
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF VERBAL ATTUNEMENT AND MIMICRY ON EMBODIED AI EMPATHY
slides.highlight: This study examines how verbal attunement and behavioral mimicry affect the perceived empathy and humanness of embodied AI agents, providing insights for RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Verbal attunement, not behavioral mimicry, is the primary driver of perceived empathy in VR AI agents.
card.key_idea: An embodied AI counselor combining GPT-4o mini with real-time facial, head, and posture mimicry to test effects of verbal vs. nonverbal synchrony.
card.evaluation: 2x2 within-subjects study (N=20) using ANOVA and correlations. Results show verbal attunement significantly increased empathy; mimicry marginally increased humanness.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=20) and exploratory gender-stratified analysis limit the generalizability of the findings.

slides.title: Identity Continuity in Long-Term Embodied AI Relationships: From Agent-Specific Identity Representation to Identity-Continuity Appraisal
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR IDENTITY CONTINUITY IN LONG-TERM EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for maintaining identity continuity in embodied AI through perceptual, behavioral, and autobiographical domains, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for maintaining perceived identity continuity in embodied AI through long-term updates and migrations.
card.key_idea: Identity is represented via three weighted domains: embodied-perceptual, psychological-behavioral, and relational-autobiographical, allowing users to judge continuity after system changes.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control
slides.tldr: CAPABILITY-AWARE SHARED CONTROL FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that balances human intent and robot capability to adapt authority, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: A shared-control framework that prevents over-helping by combining semantic intent confidence with VLA capability confidence.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM for intent inference (with Bayesian filtering) and a VLA for actions, blending authority via a sigmoid mapping of both confidence signals and human-robot disagreement.
card.evaluation: Tested with 12 participants on pick-and-place/stacking tasks (ID and OOD). Achieved 92% success rate, outperforming manual teleoperation (83%) and intent-only arbitration (44%).
card.limitation: Bayesian filtering creates a trade-off between temporal stability and responsiveness to genuine intent changes; VLA may not align with individual motion preferences.

slides.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE OPINION DYNAMICS IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to separate belief from speech, allowing for auditable and controllable opinion dynamics in social simulations. This supports MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: BCA adds a Bayesian belief layer to LLM agents for controllable, auditable social simulations.
card.key_idea: Separates latent belief (Beta distribution) from language generation; updates beliefs via a Bayesian step with a stubbornness parameter $\kappa$ mapping to classical opinion dynamics.
card.evaluation: Tested on four LLMs (GPT-5.4, Llama-4, Claude) using synthetic policy questions; validated via $\kappa$-recovery (Spearman 1.0) and FJ fixed-point matching ($R^2=0.93-0.99$).
card.limitation: Uses a single synthetic topic and complete graph; results are not predictions of human opinion change.

slides.title: RoboCafé in the Open: Interaction Continuity in Long-Term Public Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: LONG-TERM PUBLIC HRI CONTINUITY
slides.highlight: This research identifies four design requirements for maintaining interaction continuity in long-term public human-robot interactions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: RoboCafé identifies four key system requirements for maintaining interaction continuity in long-term public HRI.
card.key_idea: An LLM-powered coffee robot using task-aware dialogue, multimodal perception, and email-based memory to study how context persists across repeated public encounters.
card.evaluation: Deployed for 12 days in a university building; 148 orders from 108 customers; analyzed via video and system logs.
card.limitation: Email-based identification was unreliable (60% missed return visits), and the system lacked multi-party speaker attribution.

slides.title: MIRA: Real-Time Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction for Embodied Companions
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME FULL-DUPLEX EMBODIED INTERACTION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: MIRA enables real-time, full-duplex interaction for embodied companions through a unified framework for streaming speech inference and generative co-speech motion. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: MIRA enables real-time, full-duplex human-robot interaction with synchronized, interruptible co-speech motion on humanoid robots.
card.key_idea: A framework combining CORTEX (dual-timescale interaction policy), ROSCO (prefix-conditioned diffusion model for streaming audio-to-motion), and RHPC (inference scheme for bounded physical commitment).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT dataset and Astribot S1 robot; showed competitive audio-motion alignment and effective streaming responsiveness/interruption handling.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Neither Silence nor Overlap Is Failure: Intent-Conditioned Evaluation of Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.tldr: INTENT-CONDITIONED TURN-TAKING EVALUATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces TACT, a benchmark that uses intent-conditioned timing kernels to evaluate turn-taking in spoken dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TACT introduces an intent-conditioned benchmark for full-duplex dialogue, replacing binary timing windows with continuous scoring.
card.key_idea: Uses a strictly proper threshold-weighted continuous ranked probability score (twCRPS) conditioned on six latent speaker intents and per-speaker memory profiles to evaluate turn-taking timing.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 11 systems on 9,728 episodes from five corpora; TACT showed Spearman 0.81 correlation with human judgments, significantly outperforming binary metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on a discretized six-class intent taxonomy and English-fitted kernels, with potential label noise and judge-model bias.

slides.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE FEEDBACK REDUCES COGNITIVE OFFLOADING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that metacognitive feedback can reduce cognitive offloading to LLMs and improve performance, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive feedback reduces cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improves subsequent unaided skill performance.
card.key_idea: Comparing metacognitive feedback (making AI-use implications explicit) and effort-based rewards (incentivizing less assistance) to prevent deskilling during fraction arithmetic practice with an LLM.
card.evaluation: Preregistered online experiment (N=704) using a 2x2-plus-control design. Measured answer offloading and unaided test performance; results showed metacognitive feedback was effective, while rewards were not.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Adaptive Scaffolding Needs Contingency: An AI Tutor That Escalates and Fades on What the Learner Does
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE AI TUTORING VIA PRESERVED METACOGNITIVE DEMAND
slides.highlight: The CoMeT system implements adaptive scaffolding that adjusts support based on learner decision points, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and monitor partner intent.

card.one_liner: CoMeT is an AI tutor that adjusts support levels based on learner performance to preserve metacognitive demand.
card.key_idea: Implements a support ladder that escalates help when learners stall and fades (resets) when they demonstrate engagement or resolve a decision point.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study with 131 adult learners on Python tasks. CoMeT matched the high demand of question-only tutors while reducing learner frustration.
card.limitation: Learners often did not answer the tutor directly, requiring the system to infer 'take-up' from substantive turns or model judgments.

slides.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
slides.tldr: SPEAKER-CENTERED MEMORY FOR MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: SpeakerMem-R1 uses a dual-track memory system to improve message attribution and relational understanding in multi-party settings. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and listener modeling within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: SpeakerMem-R1 improves multi-party dialogue memory using a dual-track system for better message attribution and state reconstruction.
card.key_idea: A dual-track memory combining verbatim messages with structured person-level and group-level views, optimized via a Writer-R1 model trained with SpeakerLevenshtein and speaker-conditioned GRPO.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on GroupMemBench, SocialMemBench, and EverMemBench using binary accuracy and token-F1; outperformed mainstream frameworks and achieved 62.33% on EverMemBench leaderboard.
card.limitation: Assumes reliable rosters and temporal identification; struggles with aliases, membership changes, implicit audiences, and parallel events.

slides.title: MSI-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Speaker Voice Interaction for Collaborative AI Agents
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTI-SPEAKER VOICE INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for multi-speaker voice interaction, identifying critical needs for speaker-grounded perception and conversational restraint relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: MSI-Bench evaluates AI voice agents' ability to handle multi-speaker memory, instruction following, and reasoning.
card.key_idea: A bilingual benchmark of 1,152 scripted audio scenes using atomic rubrics to test speaker-grounded perception, authority tracking, and conversational restraint in collaborative settings.
card.evaluation: 12 models (including Gemini, GPT, Qwen) were tested. Results show low reliability, with the strongest English configuration passing only 66.8% of cases.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized, scripted speech and lacks positive cases for selective engagement during bystander interruptions.

slides.title: Toward Human-in-the-Loop Robot Failure Recovery: Bridging Communication Gaps in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING ROBOT FAILURE RECOVERY COMMUNICATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces LD-HRI to evaluate how robots can bridge communication gaps when asking humans for help during failure recovery, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: LD-HRI is a benchmark and dataset evaluating robot help requests across varying levels of listener knowledge.
card.key_idea: A web-based communication game manipulating control-interface, robot-part, and scene information to test how expert vs. novice listener knowledge affects failure recovery success.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 446 human requests and 1,302 trials (240 participants), plus 560 trials with 24 LLM requests; measured via task success and NASA-TLX.
card.limitation: LLM and human studies were collected separately, meaning the results do not establish a causal advantage for either speaker type.

slides.title: LLM-based Conversational AI Knowledge Assistant for MyBuddy Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: LLM-POWERED KNOWLEDGE ASSISTANT FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work implements an LLM-based conversational assistant for a humanoid robot to enable natural, context-aware interaction and knowledge retrieval, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: An LLM-powered conversational assistant for the MyBuddy humanoid robot enabling real-time, knowledge-rich speech interactions.
card.key_idea: A cascading speech-to-speech architecture integrating Whisper-Fast (ASR), Llama 3.1 8B via Agno agent with internet tool-calling (Wikipedia, arXiv, Google), and Kokoro-82M (TTS).
card.evaluation: Qualitative dialogue tests on diverse topics and quantitative execution time measurements (12s to 42s per response) using a GPU PC.
card.limitation: Response latency varies significantly based on query complexity and the need for external web searches.

slides.title: HINT-Blimp: Human INTent Inference from Multimodal Cues for Robotic Blimps
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL INTENT INFERENCE FOR ROBOTIC BLIMPS
slides.highlight: This research introduces a framework for inferring human intent via physical pushes and spoken commands, contributing to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework for robotic blimps to infer human navigation intent from pushes and voice commands.
card.key_idea: Human intent is modeled as a parameterized linear dynamical system (LDS) and estimated online using a particle filter that fuses physical pushes and directional hints.
card.evaluation: Tested on a physical blimp with 5 participants over 300 trials; combined modalities achieved 86% goal identification, often within two interactions.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Hero Esports Launches International Humanoid Robot Sports League
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT SPORTS LEAGUE LAUNCH
slides.highlight: The launch of an international humanoid robot sports league provides a new context for exploring embodied social robots and human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Chinese Startup Spirit AI Predicts Humanoid Robots Following Verbal Commands by Mid-2027
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTS WITH VERBAL COMMANDS BY 2027
slides.highlight: Spirit AI predicts the arrival of humanoid robots capable of following verbal commands by mid-2027, which relates to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Open Questions Towards Skill-Sustaining Reliance in Reflective AI Engagement
slides.tldr: SUSTAINING HUMAN AGENCY IN REFLECTIVE AI ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This work explores reflective mechanisms and metacognition to reduce overreliance and sustain human agency over time, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: The paper explores whether reflective AI engagement mechanisms can sustain professional expertise and agency long-term.
card.key_idea: It identifies four challenges: individual differences in reflective support, friction in efficiency-driven workflows, potential metacognitive deskilling, and the gap between short-term evidence and long-term claims.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper is a discussion/position piece raising open research questions based on a review of prior literature.
card.limitation: Current evidence primarily relies on short-term, single-session studies, leaving long-term effects on skill sustainability unknown.

slides.title: Object-Centered Reconstruction for Vision-Based 3D Force Estimation
slides.tldr: VISION-BASED 3D FORCE ESTIMATION FROM TISSUE DEFORMATION
slides.highlight: This work proposes a vision-based pipeline to estimate 3D interaction forces from soft-tissue deformation, supporting the MOSAIC goal of physics and force-based human proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: A vision-based pipeline estimating 3D interaction forces from soft-tissue deformation in stereo endoscopic video.
card.key_idea: Reconstructs tissue point clouds in an object-centered coordinate frame, tracks points using geometry-constrained SIREN optimization, and regresses force via a Set Transformer and LSTM.
card.evaluation: Tested on rubber-glove phantoms and ex vivo porcine colons using RMSE and R². Achieved average RMSEs of 0.77N and 1.30N, respectively.
card.limitation: End-to-end speed is limited to 1 FPS due to depth estimation; object-frame definition assumes long, tubular anatomy.

slides.title: Inferring the microscopic mechanisms of opinion dynamics using a kinetic Ising model
slides.tldr: EMPIRICAL VALIDATION OF KINETIC ISING MODELS FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research provides empirical support for using kinetic Ising models to describe binary opinion dynamics in online social networks. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and the modeling of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Empirical data from Twitter climate debates validates that kinetic Ising models accurately describe binary opinion dynamics.
card.key_idea: A hierarchy of kinetic Ising models was used to infer transition probabilities, revealing that opinion persistence is strongly correlated with node degree and network heterogeneity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a year-long Twitter dataset (165.4k accounts) via log-loss and Monte Carlo simulations; M4 (degree-dependent persistence) achieved the best predictive performance.
card.limitation: The analysis identifies correlations between network topology and persistence but does not establish the direction of causality.
